description: One entry per layer blend mode with its per-channel formula (B = base/underlying value, S = blend/source layer value, both normalised 0-1), what it is used for, its Shift+Alt shortcut (Move tool or any non-painting tool active) and its ExtendScript/UXP enum name. The same modes are available for brushes, layer styles, Fill/Stroke, Apply Image and Calculations.

tools.name: Normal (blend mode)
tools.description: The default: the layer's pixels simply cover the layers beneath, with Opacity and Fill controlling how much shows through. Result = S. In Bitmap or Indexed Color documents it is called Threshold.
tools.usage: Layers panel > blend mode menu > Normal   |   Shift+Alt+N   |   BlendMode.NORMAL
tools.example:
layer.blendMode = BlendMode.NORMAL;   // ExtendScript
// UXP: layer.blendMode = require('photoshop').constants.BlendMode.NORMAL;
tools.notes: Opacity and Fill behave identically in Normal mode.

tools.name: Dissolve (blend mode)
tools.description: Replaces a random subset of underlying pixels with the layer's pixels, the proportion set by the opacity, with no anti-aliasing. At 100 % it looks identical to Normal; lower opacities give a speckled, grainy dither. Used for spray-paint edges, sparkles and retro dithered transparency.
tools.usage: Layers panel > Dissolve   |   Shift+Alt+I   |   BlendMode.DISSOLVE
tools.example:
1. Duplicate a soft-edged glow layer.
2. Set blend mode Dissolve, opacity 40 %, then Gaussian Blur the copy 1 px for a grainy glow.
tools.notes: Only visible on semi-transparent pixels or at reduced opacity; the pattern is fixed per position, not animated.

tools.name: Darken (blend mode)
tools.description: Keeps whichever value is darker per channel: result = min(B, S). Lighter parts of the layer disappear, so white is neutral. Used to drop a signature on white paper onto an image, to combine multiple exposures keeping the darker sky, and in Apply Image for masks.
tools.usage: Layers panel > Darken   |   Shift+Alt+K   |   BlendMode.DARKEN
tools.example: Place a scanned black-ink signature on a white background above the photo and set it to Darken - the paper vanishes.
tools.notes: Because it works per channel it can shift colours; Darker Color compares the composite instead.

tools.name: Multiply (blend mode)
tools.description: Multiplies the values: result = B x S, always darker (like stacking two slides). White is neutral, black stays black. The workhorse for shadows, ink line-art over colour, burning in with a painted layer and overlaying scanned textures.
tools.usage: Layers panel > Multiply   |   Shift+Alt+M   |   BlendMode.MULTIPLY
tools.notes: Duplicating a layer in Multiply is a fast way to darken a washed-out scan. Commutative: layer order does not matter.

tools.name: Color Burn (blend mode)
tools.description: Darkens the base by increasing contrast toward the blend colour: result = 1 - (1 - B) / S. Produces saturated, crunchy darks and clips quickly; white is neutral. Used for intense colour tinting of shadows and gritty texture blends.
tools.usage: Layers panel > Color Burn   |   Shift+Alt+B   |   BlendMode.COLORBURN
tools.example: Fill a layer with a deep blue, set to Color Burn at 30 % Fill to cool and deepen shadows without touching highlights.
tools.notes: One of the eight 'special' modes where Fill and Opacity give different results - lower Fill for a gentler effect.

tools.name: Linear Burn (blend mode)
tools.description: Darkens by decreasing brightness: result = B + S - 1, clipped at 0. Darker than Multiply and less saturated than Color Burn; white is neutral. Often used with textures and for drawing crisp dark line work.
tools.usage: Layers panel > Linear Burn   |   Shift+Alt+A   |   BlendMode.LINEARBURN
tools.example: Grunge texture layer set to Linear Burn at 40 % opacity over a poster.
tools.notes: Special (Fill differs from Opacity). Exact inverse of Linear Dodge.

tools.name: Darker Color (blend mode)
tools.description: Compares the total luminance of the blend and base pixels and shows the darker of the two whole pixels, without mixing channels. Unlike Darken it never invents new colours, which makes it useful for compositing multiple exposures and for cleaner keying.
tools.usage: Layers panel > Darker Color   |   (no default shortcut)   |   BlendMode.DARKERCOLOR
tools.example: Stack two frames of a time-lapse and set the top to Darker Color to keep the darker silhouettes from both.
tools.notes: Introduced in CS3. Not offered as a brush mode; available for layers, layer styles and Apply Image.

tools.name: Lighten (blend mode)
tools.description: Keeps whichever value is lighter per channel: result = max(B, S). Black is neutral. Used to stack light trails, fireworks and star-trail frames, and to place white line-art on black over a photo.
tools.usage: Layers panel > Lighten   |   Shift+Alt+G   |   BlendMode.LIGHTEN
tools.example: File > Scripts > Load Files into Stack, select all layers, set them to Lighten: a star-trail composite.
tools.notes: Per-channel; Lighter Color compares composite luminance.

tools.name: Screen (blend mode)
tools.description: Multiplies the inverses: result = 1 - (1 - B)(1 - S), always lighter (like projecting two slides on one screen). Black is neutral. The standard mode for glows, lens flares, light leaks, fog and any black-background element.
tools.usage: Layers panel > Screen   |   Shift+Alt+S   |   BlendMode.SCREEN
tools.example: Place a black-background 'light leak' JPEG as a layer and set it to Screen; the black disappears leaving only the light.
tools.notes: Duplicating a dark image in Screen brightens it like a one-stop exposure push.

tools.name: Color Dodge (blend mode)
tools.description: Brightens the base by decreasing contrast toward the blend colour: result = B / (1 - S). Produces glowing, saturated highlights that clip fast; black is neutral. Popular for painting light sources, neon and 'glowing' rim light with a soft brush.
tools.usage: Layers panel > Color Dodge   |   Shift+Alt+D   |   BlendMode.COLORDODGE
tools.example: New layer set to Color Dodge, paint with a large soft brush in warm orange at 10 % flow over the light source.
tools.notes: Special mode: use Fill instead of Opacity to tame it without changing its character.

tools.name: Linear Dodge (Add) (blend mode)
tools.description: Adds the values: result = B + S, clipped at 1. Brighter than Screen, and the mathematically correct way to combine light contributions (render passes, additive light). Black is neutral.
tools.usage: Layers panel > Linear Dodge (Add)   |   Shift+Alt+W   |   BlendMode.LINEARDODGE
tools.example: Stack diffuse, specular and emissive render passes as layers; set the upper passes to Linear Dodge (Add) to rebuild the beauty pass.
tools.notes: Special mode. In 32-bit linear documents Add behaves exactly as in a renderer.

tools.name: Lighter Color (blend mode)
tools.description: Shows whichever whole pixel (blend or base) has the higher composite luminance, without mixing channels. Cleaner than Lighten for stacking exposures where you want no colour contamination.
tools.usage: Layers panel > Lighter Color   |   (no default shortcut)   |   BlendMode.LIGHTERCOLOR
tools.example: Two lightning frames stacked; the top set to Lighter Color keeps both bolts intact.
tools.notes: Not offered as a brush mode.

tools.name: Overlay (blend mode)
tools.description: Multiplies dark base values and screens light ones, using the base to decide: Multiply where B < 0.5, Screen where B > 0.5. 50 % grey is neutral, so it boosts contrast and saturation while keeping highlights and shadows. The default for dodge-and-burn grey layers, texture overlays and High Pass sharpening.
tools.usage: Layers panel > Overlay   |   Shift+Alt+O   |   BlendMode.OVERLAY
tools.example: Layer > New > Layer..., Mode Overlay, tick 'Fill with Overlay-neutral color (50% gray)', then paint white/black at low opacity to dodge and burn.
tools.notes: Overlay is Hard Light with the layers swapped. Fill and Opacity are equivalent here.

tools.name: Soft Light (blend mode)
tools.description: A gentler Overlay: darkens where S < 0.5 and lightens where S > 0.5 with a smooth curve that never clips to pure black or white. 50 % grey is neutral. Preferred for subtle contrast, gradient vignettes, colour toning and gentle texture.
tools.usage: Layers panel > Soft Light   |   Shift+Alt+F   |   BlendMode.SOFTLIGHT
tools.example: Duplicate the image, Filter > Blur > Gaussian Blur 30 px, set to Soft Light 50 % - the classic 'Orton' glow.
tools.notes: Formula (Photoshop): S<=0.5: B - (1-2S)B(1-B); S>0.5: B + (2S-1)(D(B)-B), where D(B) is a sqrt-based curve.

tools.name: Hard Light (blend mode)
tools.description: Multiplies or screens depending on the blend layer: Multiply where S < 0.5, Screen where S > 0.5. Harsher than Overlay because the top layer drives the result; 50 % grey is neutral. Used for strong texture stamping and for Emboss/High Pass results that need more punch.
tools.usage: Layers panel > Hard Light   |   Shift+Alt+H   |   BlendMode.HARDLIGHT
tools.example: Filter > Stylize > Emboss on a duplicate, then Hard Light to add crisp relief.
tools.notes: Hard Light on top = Overlay with layers swapped.

tools.name: Vivid Light (blend mode)
tools.description: Color Burn where S < 0.5 and Color Dodge where S > 0.5, i.e. contrast-based burning and dodging in one mode. Very strong and saturated; 50 % grey is neutral. Used for punchy High Pass sharpening and dramatic texture.
tools.usage: Layers panel > Vivid Light   |   Shift+Alt+V   |   BlendMode.VIVIDLIGHT
tools.example: High Pass (3 px) layer set to Vivid Light at 40 % Fill for aggressive detail enhancement.
tools.notes: Special mode (Fill differs from Opacity).

tools.name: Linear Light (blend mode)
tools.description: Linear Burn where S < 0.5 and Linear Dodge where S > 0.5: result = B + 2S - 1. 50 % grey is neutral and the response is perfectly linear, which is why frequency-separation retouching uses it to recombine the high-frequency layer exactly.
tools.usage: Layers panel > Linear Light   |   Shift+Alt+J   |   BlendMode.LINEARLIGHT
tools.example: Frequency separation (8-bit): Apply Image on the High layer with Subtract, Scale 2, Offset 128, then set High to Linear Light - the image reconstructs pixel-perfectly.
tools.notes: Special mode. For 16-bit frequency separation use Apply Image with Add, Scale 2, Offset 0 and Invert ticked.

tools.name: Pin Light (blend mode)
tools.description: Replaces colours depending on the blend value: Darken where S < 0.5 (keeps base pixels lighter than S), Lighten where S > 0.5. Effectively a hard-edged Overlay that produces posterised, patchy results; used mainly for special effects and noise textures.
tools.usage: Layers panel > Pin Light   |   Shift+Alt+Z   |   BlendMode.PINLIGHT
tools.example: Add Noise layer set to Pin Light for a grainy, high-contrast texture.
tools.notes: 50 % grey is neutral.

tools.name: Hard Mix (blend mode)
tools.description: Adds the channel values of blend and base and thresholds each channel to 0 or 255, so the result contains only the eight primary/secondary colours plus black and white. Lowering Fill softens the threshold into a contrast boost, which is how it is used for gritty texture and extreme local contrast.
tools.usage: Layers panel > Hard Mix   |   Shift+Alt+L   |   BlendMode.HARDMIX
tools.example: Duplicate a portrait, Hard Mix, Fill 15 % - a strong, edgy contrast/detail effect; mask off skin.
tools.notes: Special mode: the Fill slider changes the threshold behaviour rather than just fading.

tools.name: Difference (blend mode)
tools.description: Subtracts the darker from the lighter: result = |B - S|. Identical pixels become black, so it is the standard way to align two layers (move until the overlap goes black), to compare two versions of a file, or to invert with a white layer. Black is neutral.
tools.usage: Layers panel > Difference   |   Shift+Alt+E   |   BlendMode.DIFFERENCE
tools.example: Set the top of two 'identical' exports to Difference and run Image > Adjustments > Levels - any non-black pixel is a difference.
tools.notes: Special mode. Filter > Render > Difference Clouds uses this internally.

tools.name: Exclusion (blend mode)
tools.description: A lower-contrast Difference: result = B + S - 2BS. White inverts the base, black is neutral, mid-tones produce muted grey. Used for faded, cross-processed colour effects with solid-colour or gradient layers.
tools.usage: Layers panel > Exclusion   |   Shift+Alt+X   |   BlendMode.EXCLUSION
tools.example: Solid Color fill layer (dark navy) set to Exclusion for a lifted, matte-shadow film look.
tools.notes: Commutative like Difference.

tools.name: Subtract (blend mode)
tools.description: Subtracts the blend value from the base: result = B - S, clipped at 0. Unlike Difference it is directional, so it can remove a known component (flat-field, gradient, lens vignette) from an image. Black is neutral.
tools.usage: Layers panel > Subtract   |   (no default shortcut)   |   BlendMode.SUBTRACT
tools.example: Blurred copy of a scan set to Subtract, then Levels: leaves only the fine detail (a manual high-pass).
tools.notes: Introduced in CS5. Also available in Apply Image/Calculations with Scale and Offset.

tools.name: Divide (blend mode)
tools.description: Divides the base by the blend: result = B / S, brightening wherever the blend is darker than white. White is neutral. Dividing an image by a blurred copy of itself removes uneven lighting and colour casts (flat-field correction, cleaning up photographed documents).
tools.usage: Layers panel > Divide   |   (no default shortcut)   |   BlendMode.DIVIDE
tools.example: Duplicate a photographed page, Gaussian Blur 50 px, set the copy to Divide - the paper becomes evenly white.
tools.notes: Introduced in CS5. Easily clips highlights; pair with a Levels layer.

tools.name: Hue (blend mode)
tools.description: Takes the hue of the blend layer with the saturation and luminance of the base. Grey (zero-saturation) base areas stay grey. Used to recolour objects while keeping their shading and to shift colour casts locally with a painted layer.
tools.usage: Layers panel > Hue   |   Shift+Alt+U   |   BlendMode.HUE
tools.example: New layer in Hue mode, paint red over a blue car: the car becomes red with the original shading intact.
tools.notes: Has no effect on greyscale base pixels. In HSL blend modes the layer order matters.

tools.name: Saturation (blend mode)
tools.description: Takes the saturation of the blend layer with the hue and luminance of the base. Painting with pure grey desaturates the base; painting with a vivid colour boosts saturation without changing hue. A precise local saturation brush.
tools.usage: Layers panel > Saturation   |   Shift+Alt+T   |   BlendMode.SATURATION
tools.example: Layer filled with 50 % grey set to Saturation: the whole image becomes monochrome; mask it to keep colour in the subject.
tools.notes: Zero-saturation blend colours yield grey regardless of their hue.

tools.name: Color (blend mode)
tools.description: Takes the hue and saturation of the blend layer with the luminance of the base, so it colourises without altering tonal detail. The classic mode for hand-colouring black-and-white photos, tinting, and for adjustment layers that should not change luminosity.
tools.usage: Layers panel > Color   |   Shift+Alt+C   |   BlendMode.COLOR
tools.example: Empty layer in Color mode, brush skin tone at 20 % opacity over a scanned B&W portrait.
tools.notes: Set Hue/Saturation and Color Balance adjustment layers to Color to prevent unintended luminosity shifts.

tools.name: Luminosity (blend mode)
tools.description: Takes the luminance of the blend layer with the hue and saturation of the base, so tonal changes never shift colour. Standard for Curves/Levels adjustment layers, for sharpening layers and High Pass to avoid halos and saturation drift.
tools.usage: Layers panel > Luminosity   |   Shift+Alt+Y   |   BlendMode.LUMINOSITY
tools.example: curvesLayer.blendMode = BlendMode.LUMINOSITY;   // contrast without saturation increase
tools.notes: Inverse of Color. Smart Filter blending can also be set to Luminosity (double-click the icon next to the filter).

tools.name: Pass Through (group blend mode)
tools.description: The default blend mode of a layer group: the group has no compositing of its own, so adjustment layers and blend modes inside it affect everything below the group. Change a group to Normal (or any other mode) to make the group composite as one unit - clipping adjustments to its contents and letting the group's opacity and mode apply to the merged result.
tools.usage: Layers panel > select a group > blend mode menu > Pass Through   |   BlendMode.PASSTHROUGH (LayerSet only)
tools.example: A group containing a subject and a Curves layer: set the group to Normal so the Curves layer affects only the subject, not the background.
tools.notes: Knockout options and Blend If also behave differently for Pass Through vs Normal groups.

tools.name: Behind and Clear (painting blend modes)
tools.description: Two modes available only for painting tools, Fill and Stroke (not layers): Behind paints only on transparent pixels, as if painting on the back of a transparent sheet, and Clear erases to transparency like the Eraser. Both require Lock Transparent Pixels to be off and do not work on the Background layer.
tools.usage: Options bar > Mode > Behind (Shift+Alt+Q) / Clear (Shift+Alt+R)   |   ColorBlendMode.BEHIND / ColorBlendMode.CLEAR (Selection.fill / stroke)
tools.example: Paint a coloured backdrop behind a cut-out character on the same layer: Brush tool, Mode Behind.
tools.notes: Clear is also available for Edit > Fill and the Paint Bucket. These two modes exist in the ColorBlendMode enum used by Selection.fill(), not in BlendMode.
